1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("starwars")
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x = eye_color))+geom_bar()
```

3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color))+geom_bar(fill="Purple", color="Black")+labs(title = "Frequency of Eye Colors in Star Wars Characters", x = "Eye Color Type", y= "Amount of Eye Colors")+theme_minimal()
```

4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x=height, fill=homeworld))+geom_histogram()
```

5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(starwars, aes(x=height, fill=homeworld))+geom_histogram()+labs(title = "Height Characters from Each Homeworld", x = "Height (cm) of Characters per Homeworld", y= "# of Characters")+scale_fill_viridis(discrete=TRUE, option="magma", name="Homeworlds")+theme_minimal()
```

6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point()
```

7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+geom_point(color="violet")+labs(title= "Starwars Character Heights by their Mass", x = "Height in CM", y= "Weight in KG")+scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2000, by=100))+theme_minimal()
```

8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=gender))+geom_point()
```

9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color=gender))+geom_point()+scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2000, by=100))+theme_minimal()+labs(title = "Starwars Character Heights by their Mass with Gender Expression", x = "Height in Centimeters (CM)", y= "Weight in Kilograms (KG) ")+theme(legend.position ="top")+scale_color_manual(values=c("deeppink2", "cornflowerblue"), name="Gender Expression")
```
